synthesis.data_playbook:
PRIMARY = FastF1 (per-lap timing/stint/compound/tyre-life/track-status/telemetry). SECONDARY = Jolpica-Ergast (api.jolpi.ca) for pit-stop DURATIONS and official results FastF1 does not surface cleanly.

INSTALL & CACHE (mandatory): `pip install fastf1` (3.8.x). At startup ONCE: `import fastf1; fastf1.Cache.enable_cache('~/fastf1_cache')` — required for speed and to avoid upstream rate limits; first telemetry pull is slow, re-runs hit disk.

LOAD: `session = fastf1.get_session(2024, 'Bahrain', 'R'); session.load(); laps = session.laps` (Laps = pandas.DataFrame subclass). session.load() pulls laps+telemetry+weather+race-control from F1 live timing.

KEY COLUMNS for deg calibration: LapTime (timedelta), LapNumber, Stint (int), Compound (SOFT/MEDIUM/HARD/INTERMEDIATE/WET/UNKNOWN), TyreLife (true tyre age incl. pre-data laps — USE THIS not lap-in-stint), FreshTyre (bool), PitInTime/PitOutTime (session-time timedeltas, non-null marks stint boundary), TrackStatus (CONCATENATED codes for the lap), IsAccurate (bool — critical filter), Deleted/DeletedReason, Sector1/2/3Time, SpeedI1/I2/FL/ST (km/h for the straightline overtaking modifier), Driver, Team, Position.

CLEAN DATASET (one line):
`clean = laps.pick_wo_box().pick_track_status('1', how='equals').pick_quicklaps(1.07)` then keep `IsAccurate==True` and drop Compound=='UNKNOWN'. This drops in/out laps, all non-green laps, and 107% outliers. Convert times via `.dt.total_seconds()`.
TrackStatus codes: 1=green, 2=yellow, 4=SafetyCar, 5=Red, 6=VSC deployed, 7=VSC ending (3 unused). Because codes are CONCATENATED within a lap, use how='contains'/'excludes' to catch partial-SC laps, not just equals.
Useful Laps methods: pick_drivers(), pick_compounds(), pick_track_status(status, how=...), pick_wo_box(), pick_box_laps(), pick_fastest(), pick_quicklaps(threshold=1.07).
Weather (~1/min): AirTemp, TrackTemp, Humidity, Rainfall, WindSpeed — use TrackTemp to flag overheating-prone deg.

FIT PROCEDURE: group clean laps by (Driver, Stint, Compound). FUEL-CORRECT FIRST: subtract k_fuel*remaining_fuel_kg (k_fuel=0.03, burn ~1.6 kg/lap) before attributing residual slope to tyre — otherwise fuel burn-off (car ~1.6 kg/lap lighter) masks/biases the deg signal. Then regress corrected LapTime on TyreLife: lap_time = base_pace(compound) + deg_rate(compound)*TyreLife + (optional) k_2*TyreLife^2 for soft-compound cliff. This yields per-compound k_0/k_1/k_2 to replace the defaults.

PIT DURATIONS (Jolpica): GET `http://api.jolpi.ca/ergast/f1/{season}/{round}/pitstops/` -> each PitStop {driverId, lap, stop, time(HH:mm:ss), duration} where duration in seconds e.g. '20.006' INCLUDING pit entry/exit/red-flag. Laps endpoint `/{season}/{round}/laps/` -> Timings[]={driverId,position,time '1:37.284'}. Per-driver: `/{season}/{round}/drivers/{driverId}/laps/`.
JOLPICA LIMITS (strict): burst 4 req/s, sustained 500 req/hour unauth (some sources 200/hr); HTTP 429 on breach; pagination default 30, MAX 100/page, offset 0. A race has 1000+ lap records (2024 Bahrain total=1129) => use FastF1 for BULK per-lap timing; reserve Jolpica for pit durations + results with client-side backoff and local/ETag caching.

OFFLINE FALLBACK: once the cache folder is populated (commit it or snapshot it), all FastF1 re-runs work fully offline — no re-download. Pre-warm the cache for your target circuits/seasons before any demo. For Jolpica, persist pulled pit-stop/results JSON to disk and read locally to stay under rate limits and survive offline.

GOTCHAS: (a) all FastF1 times are Timedelta — always .total_seconds(); (b) Jolpica had reported lap-time correction issues for some 2024 races vs Ergast — cross-check FastF1 (F1 live timing) when accuracy matters; (c) Compound can be 'UNKNOWN' for some sessions — filter out; (d) Jolpica duration already includes entry/exit so don't double-count a separate pit-lane delta — but for PIT_LOSS-vs-staying-out you still need the track in/out travel penalty on top of the stationary part.
synthesis.architecture:
Package `f1strategy/` — clean, documented, PyTorch/Scikit-learn stack to mirror the Williams job spec language ("real-time simulation", "data fusion", "explainable AI", "optimisation", "anomaly detection").

f1strategy/
  core/            # Python: lap-time model, tyre/fuel/pit/SC/overtaking equations, parameter dataclasses per circuit (the L1 model). Pure-Python reference impl, fully unit-tested and readable.
  sim/             # Monte-Carlo race simulator: multi-car cumulative-time loop, ghost-car SC injection, retirement/failure sampling, vectorised NumPy for the 10k-run batch. Deterministic mode (n_runs==1) exports CSV; n_runs>1 -> outcome distributions (E[pos], P(win), CVaR).
  fastloop/        # Rust hot loop (via PyO3/maturin) reimplementing sim/'s inner per-lap multi-car update for the 10,000-iteration MC batch — Rust gives the order-of-magnitude speedup needed so live re-optimisation stays sub-second. Python core stays the source of truth; Rust is a drop-in accelerator validated bit-for-bit against it.
  optimize/        # L2: exhaustive enumerator (itertools.combinations_with_replacement, FIA 2-compound rule), convex stop-lap placement, backward-DP, and Aguad-Thraves Stackelberg DP for 2-car. Scores candidates over the MC distribution; risk-frontier selector.
  surrogate/       # PyTorch MLP (256-128-64, heteroscedastic NLL or 5-model ensemble) trained offline on sim/ outputs => <1 s full-strategy-space what-if. Optional Emukit multi-fidelity (Kennedy-O'Hagan AR1) fusion layer wrapping the cheap analytical lap model.
  live/            # Live Bayesian updater: Kalman filter (state [a,b]=fresh-pace+deg-rate) updating each lap with calibrated 90% credible bands; particle-filter upgrade path for non-Gaussian/regime-switching. Plus pit-decision re-optimiser triggered on SC/VSC. Anomaly detection (lap-time residual vs filter prediction) lives here too.
  data/            # FastF1 + Jolpica pull/clean/calibrate harness (Sec data_playbook): produces per-circuit parameter files and reports RMSPE-per-stint calibration error honestly.
  dashboard/       # Streamlit/Plotly what-if UI: pit-lap x compound heatmap of P(finish position), live tyre bands, recommendation + strategist-readable reason (feature importance) + counterfactual ("if no SC by lap 30, switch to 1-stop") + confidence. Mirrors RaceWatch's role-dashboard idea but adds the sub-second surrogate + UQ.
  tests/           # pytest: equation unit tests, Rust-vs-Python parity, calibration regression (RMSPE bounds), FIA-rule enforcement, SC-distribution sampling sanity, surrogate-vs-sim accuracy, Kalman convergence vs synthetic stints.

DATA FLOW: data/ -> per-circuit params -> core/sim/ (MC) -> surrogate/ (trained offline) + optimize/ (candidates) -> live/ (filter + re-optimise on SC) -> dashboard/. Architect every component so swapping public FastF1 data for proprietary sensor telemetry only improves it (state the residual gap explicitly). Ship in PyTorch/Scikit-learn with clean docs to match the post-Atlassian "productionise off spreadsheets" culture. Do NOT claim AWS powers team strategy (it powers FOM broadcast/IT only).
synthesis.shock_factor:
Three elements most likely to genuinely impress a Williams strategy reviewer:

1. SUB-SECOND, FULL-STRATEGY-SPACE WHAT-IF SURROGATE (the headline). Published state-space tyre models take 15-30 s/run and a classic Monte-Carlo batch needs thousands of runs per decision — too slow to sweep interactively when a safety car drops with seconds to decide. A PyTorch surrogate trained on the calibrated MC sim that returns finishing-position probability for EVERY pit-lap x compound x stop-count combination in <1 s directly attacks the real pit-wall latency pain. It mirrors the role's "real-time simulation" wording and out-thinks RaceWatch on the one axis (speed) teams actually feel. Frame: "turns a multi-second Monte-Carlo batch into a sub-second, explainable what-if you can run live on the pit wall — here are the calibration numbers proving it." Optional Rust hot loop reinforces the production-grade speed story.

2. LIVE BAYESIAN TYRE LAYER WITH CALIBRATED UNCERTAINTY, BENCHMARKED. A Kalman/particle filter updating fresh-pace + deg-rate every lap and emitting calibrated 90% credible bands (not point estimates), with state reset at pit stops, explicitly benchmarked to beat ARIMA (RMSPE ~1.08 vs 1.52 s, CRPS 0.20 vs 0.32). This is the single highest-signal, most defensible component because the published literature itself argues deep-learning tyre work "lacks interpretability and explicit uncertainty quantification — features crucial in operational race environments." Demonstrating operational UQ, not just a better point prediction, signals you understand that with margins of tenths-of-a-position, quantified uncertainty wins races.

3. ROBUST + NATIVELY EXPLAINABLE RECOMMENDER UNDER SC UNCERTAINTY. Optimise a risk-adjusted objective (CVaR / maximise P(finish ahead of rival)) across the FULL distribution of safety-car outcomes via ghost-car SC modelling — and visualise the REGRET of the naive expected-case-optimal plan when a SC actually hits. Output a recommendation PLUS a strategist-readable reason (feature importance), a counterfactual ("if no SC by lap 30, switch to 1-stop"), and a confidence band. This hits the job spec's explicit "explainable AI" and "optimisation" asks, and existing RL work (RSRL, +0.3 positions) bolts explainability on as an afterthought — a natively explainable robust recommender is both novel and exactly on-brief. Underpinning all three: a calibration harness that reports residual error HONESTLY per stint and is architected so swapping public data for proprietary telemetry only improves it — the production-data mindset that says you'd plug into real sensor streams on day one.
open_risks: k_fuel 0.107 s/kg from arXiv:2512.00640 PDF-summary is ~3x the well-established ~0.03 s/kg and almost certainly an extraction error — REJECTED; default 0.03 but re-fit per track (track range 0.019-0.036 is real and large).

ALL tyre coefficients (k_0/k_1/k_2) are circuit- AND season-specific (defaults are Spielberg/Austria-2025 derived) — MUST re-fit per event from FastF1 FP2 long-runs; do not ship the defaults to a real race.

Compound pace deltas are often statistically INDISTINCT in clean data (state-space found hard vs medium not significant) — the assumed 0.5 s/lap adjacent step may not hold; calibrate, don't assume large fixed gaps.
Per-circuit PIT_LOSS values are mostly secondary/aggregator sources (medium confidence), not official FIA pit-delta tables — validate against Jolpica pit durations + observed in/out-lap deltas.

SC/VSC probabilities are a 2014-2019 fit; recent seasons differ (2022 1.77 cautions/race vs 2024 1.13, record 9-race no-SC run) and per-circuit P(SC) varies enormously — scale to current circuit history and CHECK the official erratum Appl. Sci. 10, 5745 before locking the distributions.
Cheap-stop saving fraction (SC 40-60%, VSC 30-40%) and the absolute 7-12 s saving are rules of thumb — the per-track in/out-lap split is the accurate version; derive from data where possible.

Dirty-air magnitude in the ground-effect era is published only as downforce-% (regressing year-on-year, ~5%@20m 2022 -> ~20% 2025), NOT s/lap — must be calibrated to historical overtake counts per circuit; sign flips by track (loss high-downforce, gain low-downforce).
Overtaking thresholds t_gap_overtake were tuned to pre-2022 racing; ground-effect cars changed following dynamics — re-validate against 2022-2024 overtake counts.
Heilmeier repo cubic tyre model has a known bug (reuses quadratic coefficients) — use linear/quadratic only.

arXiv:2512.00640 uses batch HMC/Stan (not a live filter) and several of its extracted constants are summarizer-derived and unverified — the recursive Kalman/PF is YOUR adaptation; re-derive constants by fitting FastF1 yourself.

Jolpica rate limits (4 req/s, 500/hr, possibly dropping to 200/hr) and reported 2024 lap-time correction issues vs Ergast — cache aggressively, cross-check against FastF1, prefer FastF1 for bulk timing.

Public timing data is a proxy for teams' hundreds of proprietary sensors — quantify the residual calibration gap (target RMSPE ~1.0-1.5 s) and state that proprietary telemetry only improves the model; do not overclaim accuracy.
VSC can end with ~10-15 s warning, so a perfect-information sim OVERVALUES VSC stops — model the information delay or flag the optimism.
Williams strategy stack is in-house/opaque; do NOT assume AWS powers team strategy (AWS is FOM broadcast/IT only) — positioning risk if claimed.
